title: Gone, But Not Forgotten
theme: Aaliyah. Left Eye. Nate Dogg. Luther. Whitney. R&B's losses are not small — and the records they left behind refuse to be quiet about it.
narrativePurpose: Test knowledge of R&B artists who passed before their time — their defining records, chart milestones, career arcs, and the cultural weight they carried while they were here.
toneProgression: The songs and voices every fan recognizes → deeper album cuts, career turning points, and industry milestones → the facts and details only devoted fans kept close

vault.note: Digit 4 (index 3) is always visible. Vault code 2-0-0-1 — the year R&B lost Aaliyah on August 25th and Left Eye on April 25th, four months apart. Two of the most vital creative forces in the genre, gone in the same calendar year. The music stayed.

rounds.name: RADIO HITS
rounds.description: The artists and records everyone knows. The hits that defined their legacies while they were here — and define them still.

questions.question: Whitney Houston's 1990 third studio album — which produced the hit 'All the Man That I Need' — was titled what?

metadata.song: All the Man That I Need
topicTags: All the Man That I Need
metadata.fact: I'm Your Baby Tonight (1990) was Whitney Houston's third studio album. 'All the Man That I Need' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1991.
metadata.storyHook: Three albums in. Still going to number one. Whitney Houston made it look effortless.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: I'm Your Baby Tonight is Whitney Houston's third studio album (released November 1990). 'All the Man That I Need' was released December 4, 1990 as the album's second single. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I%27m_Your_Baby_Tonight, Whitney Houston official site https://www.whitneyhouston.com/news/whitney-houstons-all-the-man-that-i-need-was-released-in-december-1990/, Spotify https://open.spotify.com/track/07M76e7IXxYdnC1BBiJxEX

questions.question: Aaliyah's 2001 self-titled album was introduced to the public with which lead single, also featuring rapper Timbaland?

metadata.fact: 'We Need a Resolution' — featuring Timbaland — was released as the lead single from Aaliyah's self-titled 2001 album, the last studio album released in her lifetime.
metadata.storyHook: The last album she made. The first single from it. 'We Need a Resolution' opened a door she wouldn't get to walk through.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'We Need a Resolution' features a rap verse by Timbaland and was released April 13, 2001 as the lead single from Aaliyah's self-titled 2001 album. Sources: Aaliyah Wiki https://aaliyahdanahaughton.fandom.com/wiki/We_Need_a_Resolution, Aaliyah official Facebook https://www.facebook.com/AaliyahHaughton/posts/%EF%B8%8Fon-this-day-25-years-ago-aaliyah-released-the-lead-single-we-need-a-reso

questions.question: Marvin Gaye's 1973 album — his follow-up to What's Going On — explored themes of sexuality and sensuality. It was titled what?

metadata.fact: Let's Get It On reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1973. Its title track became one of the most recognizable songs in soul history, and the album cemented Gaye's transformation from Motown hitmaker to singular artistic voice.
metadata.storyHook: After he finished saving the world on What's Going On, Marvin Gaye had other things on his mind.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Let's Get It On (1973) is Marvin Gaye's follow-up to What's Going On, framed around themes of sexuality and sensuality. Sources: Motown classic feature https://classic.motown.com/story/marvin-gaye-gets-it-on/

sources.title: Let's Get It On – classic Motown feature

questions.question: Before launching his solo career, Luther Vandross spent years as one of the most in-demand session vocalists in New York. His 1981 debut solo album was titled what?

metadata.fact: Luther Vandross had already sung on hundreds of records, jingles, and background sessions before Never Too Much. The album debuted at #1 on the R&B albums chart and established him as a solo force immediately.
metadata.storyHook: He'd been singing on everyone else's records for years. Then he made one of his own.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Never Too Much (1981) is Luther Vandross' debut solo album and topped the R&B albums chart. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Never_Too_Much_(album)

questions.question: TLC's 'No Scrubs' — which reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1999 — appeared on which TLC album?

metadata.fact: 'No Scrubs' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1999 and became one of TLC's signature records. FanMail was their third studio album and their final record with all three members.
metadata.storyHook: Their last album with all three of them. 'No Scrubs' led the way.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'No Scrubs' is the lead single from TLC's third studio album FanMail (1999). Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No_Scrubs

questions.question: Nate Dogg's 2001 solo studio album was titled what?

metadata.fact: Music & Me (2001) is Nate Dogg's second and final studio album on Reprise Records. His debut was G-Funk Classics, Vol. 1 & 2 (1998). Music & Me showcased the hook-singing style that had made him the most sought-after voice on West Coast hip-hop and R&B records throughout the late 1990s.
metadata.storyHook: The man who sang everyone else's hooks finally got to make his own album.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Music & Me is the second and final studio album by Nate Dogg, released December 4, 2001. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_%26_Me_(Nate_Dogg_album)

questions.question: Aaliyah's 2001 hit 'Try Again' — later included on her posthumous self-titled album — originally appeared on the soundtrack to which film?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 1 OF 3 — AALIYAH'S ROMEO MUST DIE SINGLE

metadata.fact: 'Try Again' first appeared on the Romeo Must Die soundtrack (2000), produced by Timbaland. It was later included on her posthumous self-titled album released in 2001.
metadata.storyHook: The song that introduced the world to what Aaliyah and Timbaland could do together — and then ended up on something even bigger.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Try Again' first appeared on the Romeo Must Die soundtrack (2000), then on her later self-titled album. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Try_Again_(Aaliyah_song)
metadata.hostNote: This question references Aaliyah's posthumous album. Frame it matter-of-factly — the focus is the film, not her passing.

reserve.question: Barry White's Love Unlimited Orchestra reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1974 with which instrumental track?

metadata.fact: 'Love's Theme' by the Love Unlimited Orchestra hit #1 on the Hot 100 in 1974 — a rare instrumental chart-topper in the R&B era.
metadata.storyHook: No vocals. No lyrics. Just Barry White's orchestra, a string arrangement, and the top of the chart.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Love's Theme' by the Love Unlimited Orchestra hit #1 on the Hot 100 in 1974. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Love%27s_Theme

reserve.question: Sam Cooke's 1960 hit — depicting prison laborers breaking rocks — reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100. It was titled what?
choices: Bring It On Home to Me

metadata.fact: 'Chain Gang' reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1960, becoming one of Sam Cooke's defining early hits and demonstrating his crossover appeal on both pop and R&B charts.
metadata.storyHook: Sam Cooke made prison labor into a pop record. It almost went to number one.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Chain Gang' (1960) is a Sam Cooke single about prisoners on a chain gang; it reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chain_Gang_(Sam_Cooke_song)

rounds.name: DEEP CUTS
rounds.description: Career turning points, industry history, and the facts that separate casual listeners from devoted fans.

questions.question: Gerald Levert — son of O'Jays co-founder Eddie Levert — first rose to prominence as the lead vocalist of which R&B group?

metadata.fact: LeVert — Gerald, his brother Sean, and Marc Gordon — reached #1 on the R&B chart with 'Casanova' in 1987. Gerald later co-founded the supergroup LSG with Keith Sweat and Johnny Gill.
metadata.storyHook: The son of a legend who became one himself. But he did it first with his brother.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Gerald Levert first gained fame as lead singer of LeVert, the trio with his brother Sean and Marc Gordon, scoring the R&B #1 'Casanova.' Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Levert

questions.question: Phyllis Hyman's most celebrated studio album — featuring her signature track 'Old Friend' — was released in 1986 and titled what?

metadata.fact: Living All Alone (1986) is widely considered Phyllis Hyman's artistic peak. 'Old Friend' became her signature ballad — a meditation on nostalgia and loss that showcased the full depth of her instrument.
metadata.storyHook: One of the most powerful voices in R&B. One album that showed exactly what she was capable of. Not enough people heard it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Living All Alone is Phyllis Hyman's 1986 studio album on Philadelphia International Records. 'Old Friend' was the first single released from the album and became her signature song. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Living_All_Alone, YouTube Music playlist https://music.youtube.com/playlist?list=OLAK5uy_lLTg5QcRC_8q9O6BCgChICXDHDbh9e170, R&B Slow Jams Facebook group https://www.facebook.com/groups/RandBSlowJamsOldandNew/posts/7428417427203702/

sources.title: Living All Alone – full album – YouTube Music
'Old Friend' was the first single released from the 'Living All Alone' album – R&B Slow Jams group

questions.question: Marvin Gaye's 1978 double album 'Here, My Dear' was unusual — its proceeds were contractually designated to go to whom?
choices: Anna Gordy Gaye — as part of their divorce settlement

metadata.fact: Anna Gordy Gaye negotiated a divorce settlement in which Marvin's next album proceeds would satisfy his obligations. He responded by recording an extraordinarily candid double album about the marriage. She later sued claiming defamation — unsuccessfully.
metadata.storyHook: A divorce settlement became a double album. A double album became one of the most painfully honest records Marvin Gaye ever made.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: The album was created as part of Marvin Gaye's divorce settlement with Anna Gordy Gaye, who was to receive proceeds from the project. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here,_My_Dear

questions.question: Before his solo breakthrough, Luther Vandross sang background vocals on which landmark 1975 David Bowie album?

metadata.fact: Luther Vandross sang and arranged background vocals on Young Americans — including on 'Fame,' co-written with John Lennon. Official posts from the Luther Vandross estate note the syncopated backing vocal arrangement was added at his suggestion.
metadata.storyHook: Before 'Never Too Much,' there was Young Americans. Before the solo career, there was the session work.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Luther Vandross is credited with backing vocals and vocal arrangements on Young Americans (1975). Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Young_Americans, Luther Vandross official Facebook https://www.facebook.com/luthervandross/posts/as-we-celebrate-the-50th-anniversary-of-david-bowies-1975-album-young-americans-/1

sources.title: Luther Vandross – Young Americans 50th anniversary post

questions.question: Whitney Houston's 'I Have Nothing' — from The Bodyguard soundtrack, and nominated for the Best Original Song Oscar in 1994 — was produced and co-written by which artist?

metadata.fact: 'I Have Nothing' was co-written by David Foster and Linda Thompson and produced by David Foster. It was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Original Song at the 66th ceremony in 1994.
metadata.storyHook: David Foster, a power ballad, and Whitney Houston. The formula worked every time they used it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'I Have Nothing' was co-written by David Foster and Linda Thompson, produced by David Foster, and nominated for Best Original Song Oscar in 1994. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Have_Nothing

questions.question: Minnie Riperton — known for her extraordinary five-octave vocal range — reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1975 with which song?

bonus.bonusHint: DIGIT 2 OF 3 — MINNIE RIPERTON'S FIVE-OCTAVE HIT

metadata.fact: 'Lovin' You' was produced by Stevie Wonder and appeared on Minnie Riperton's 1974 album Perfect Angel. It reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in April 1975. Riperton died of breast cancer in July 1979, aged 31.
metadata.storyHook: Five octaves. One note everyone remembers. Minnie Riperton made it look like breathing.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Minnie Riperton is widely cited as having an approximately five-octave vocal range. 'Lovin' You' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1975 — the only one of the four choices to do so. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lovin%27_You_(Minnie_Riperton_song)

reserve.question: Heavy D — born Dwight Arrington Myers — was the frontman and rapper of which group?

metadata.fact: Heavy D & The Boyz were a pioneering hip-hop soul group signed to Uptown Records, blending rap with melodic R&B production and paving the way for the new jack swing movement.
metadata.storyHook: Dwight Myers walked into every room as the heaviest man in hip-hop. He filled it.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Heavy D was frontman and rapper for Heavy D & The Boyz. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_D_%26_the_Boyz

reserve.question: Donna Summer's 'Last Dance' won the Academy Award for Best Original Song in 1979. It appeared on the soundtrack to which film?

metadata.fact: 'Last Dance' was written for and appeared in the 1978 film Thank God It's Friday. It won the Oscar for Best Original Song at the 51st Academy Awards in 1979.
metadata.storyHook: A disco film nobody remembers won an Oscar nobody forgets — because Donna Summer sang the song.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: 'Last Dance' was written for and appears in the 1978 film Thank God It's Friday and won the 1979 Oscar for Best Original Song. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Last_Dance_(Donna_Summer_song)

rounds.name: HIDDEN GEMS
rounds.description: The archival level. The founders, the independent moves, and the decisions that shaped what R&B became.

questions.question: Sam Cooke co-founded his own record label in 1959 — making him one of the first Black artists to own and control his music. That label was named what?

metadata.fact: SAR Records — co-founded with manager J.W. Alexander — signed Bobby Womack's family group The Valentinos and gave Cooke direct control over his publishing and artist development. The label dissolved after Cooke's death in 1964.
metadata.storyHook: Sam Cooke didn't just make the records. He owned the company.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: In 1959 Sam Cooke co-founded SAR Records (Sam & Alex Records) with J.W. Alexander, signing groups like The Valentinos. Sources: Instagram reel https://www.instagram.com/reel/C2z56ZquhuU/?hl=en, Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAR_Records

sources.title: Sam Cooke's SAR Records label – Instagram reel

questions.question: Otis Redding co-wrote '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' — his only #1 hit — with which Stax Records guitarist, completing the recording just days before Redding's death in December 1967?

metadata.song: (Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay
metadata.fact: Redding recorded the song on December 7, 1967. He died in a plane crash on December 10. Released posthumously in January 1968, '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' became his first and only #1 hit on the Billboard Hot 100.
metadata.storyHook: Three days after recording it, Otis Redding was gone. The song spent weeks at number one without him.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' was co-written by Otis Redding and Steve Cropper, and Redding recorded it in 1967 shortly before his death. Sources: Facebook tribute post https://www.facebook.com/glencampbellofficial/posts/remembering-steve-cropper-co-writer-of-sittin-on-the-dock-of-the-bay-with-ot
metadata.hostNote: The question stem mentions Redding's death. This is factually integral. Deliver calmly and move forward.

sources.title: Remembering Steve Cropper – '(Sittin' On) The Dock of the Bay' post

questions.question: Luther Vandross won four Grammy Awards in a single night in 2004 — including Record of the Year — for his recording of which song?
choices: A House Is Not a Home

metadata.fact: Luther won four Grammys in 2004 — Record of the Year, Song of the Year (with co-writer Richard Marx), Best Male R&B Vocal Performance, and Best R&B Album — for Dance with My Father. He was too ill to attend the ceremony.
metadata.storyHook: He was too ill to attend the ceremony. The Grammys sent someone to collect his four awards anyway.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: Luther Vandross won four Grammys in 2004 including Record of the Year for 'Dance with My Father,' co-written with Richard Marx. Sources: Richard Marx Facebook https://www.facebook.com/richardmarxmusic/posts/fbf-performing-dance-with-my-father-with-c%C3%A9line-dion-at-the-2004-grammys-lu, Luther Vandross official page https://www.facebook.com/luthervandross/posts/richard-marx-performs-his-rendition-of-dance-with-my-father-a-song-he-co-wrote-w/7

Luther Vandross page – 'Dance With My Father' Grammy note

reserve.question: Whitney Houston's final studio album, released in 2009, was titled what?

metadata.fact: I Look to You (2009) is Whitney Houston's seventh and final studio album. It debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200.
metadata.storyHook: Her seventh album. Her last. Released in 2009. She didn't know it yet.
metadata.sourceNotes: Verified: I Look to You (2009) is listed as Whitney Houston's seventh and final studio album. Sources: Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I_Look_to_You
metadata.hostNote: The word 'final' is present in the question. The framing is neutral — no adjustment needed.
